o: Simulate a byte-array allocator: allocate(size, mID) finds the leftmost run of `size` free units and tags them mID; free(mID) clears all units tagged mID and returns how many were freed. Sizes, ids, and call counts are all ≤ 1000, so an O(n) scan per allocate and O(n) sweep per free — O(n²) total ≈ 10^6 ops — is perfectly fine. The example walks through interleaved allocations/frees including failed allocation (return −1) and freeing a nonexistent id (return 0).
k: Linear scan for the first run of `size` consecutive zeros; tag with mID.
free(mID): sweep the array, clear matching cells, count cleared.
Multiple blocks may share an mID; free must clear them all.

a.i: Keep an int array mem of size n (0 = free, otherwise mID). Allocate scans left to right tracking run length; free sweeps and zeroes matches.
s: allocate: scan i from 0; maintain run counter; when run reaches size, fill [start, i] with mID and return start; else −1.
freeMemory: count cells equal to mID, set them to 0, return count.
a.t: O(n) per allocate, O(n) per free — O(n·calls) total, trivial for n, calls ≤ 1000

a.n: Approach 2: Interval List + ID Map (better asymptotics)
a.i: Maintain sorted disjoint free intervals plus a map mID → allocated intervals. Allocation scans free intervals for the first with length ≥ size; free merges returned intervals back. This scales to huge n and many calls.
s: Free intervals kept in a sorted structure (list here).
allocate: find first free interval with length ≥ size, carve it, record (mID, start, len), return start.
free: look up mID's intervals, reinsert them into the free list merging neighbors, return total length.
a.t: O(F) per allocate (F = free-interval count), O(B + F) per free

w: Given the tiny constraints, the flat array is the pragmatic interview answer — say so explicitly, then offer the interval design as the scalable follow-up. Pitfalls: resetting the run counter correctly on occupied cells, handling free of unknown mID (return 0), and remembering allocate fills the LEFTMOST fit (first-fit, not best-fit). Follow-up: implement best-fit, or support allocate with alignment requirements.
